summary: Haeju Sunim works in Buddhist studies. She served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and was attested as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Dongguk University in 1999.

Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed an MA at Peking University under Kemo Jin (ending 1982) and studied under Zhongxin Jiang, later holding posts at the University of Vienna (attested 1996) and University of Freiburg (Director, 2010).

Hajime Kitamura was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Shizuoka High School, University of Tokyo, and under Tokan Tada. His posts included Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986), Reitaku University president (~1986–1994), and Toyo Bunko board chair (1990–2001).

Hajime Nakamura specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo under Hakuju Ui, served as an associate professor there (1943–1973), and founded and directed the Eastern Institute and Tōhō Gakuin (1973–1999).

Hajime Okayama worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, Peking University, and CASS under Xianlin Ji. He held academic positions at the University of Tokyo (1988, 1990, 1995–2012) and its Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (~1986–2013).

Hajime Sakurabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated through his PhD at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, he held multiple academic positions there between 1949 and 1986, as well as teaching at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1960).

Hajime Tanabe was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University, Berlin, and Freiburg, studying under Kitarō Nishida, Edmund Husserl, Heinrich Rickert, and Martin Heidegger. He held posts at Tohoku University (1913) and Kyoto University (1919–1945).
Hakuin Ekaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Dōkyō Etan (~1708) and Hakuyūshi (~1710–1711), and taught Suiō Genro.

Hakuju Ui was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu, as well as at Tübingen under Richard von Garbe, Oxford, and Cambridge. He held teaching posts at Tokyo, Tohoku, Komazawa, and Nagoya universities.

Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Toshima Normal School and trained under Sogaku Daiun Harada and Genpo Tsuyama, among others, later founding Sanbo Zen in 1954.
Halle O'Neal works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Kansas under the supervision of Sherry Fowler (attested 2011).

Hammalawa Saddhatissa worked in Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Banaras Hindu University and the University of Edinburgh. He served as head of the London Buddhist Vihara (1957–1985) and taught at Banaras Hindu University, SOAS, and the University of Toronto (1966–1969).
Hank Glassman works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, holding a faculty post at Haverford College (attested 2009 and 2019).

Hanns Oertel was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Yale University under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale (1891–1917), the University of Marburg (1922), and held the chair of Indian and Iranian philology at the University of Munich (1925–1935).

Hanns-Peter Schmidt was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf and served as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles from 1965 to 2000.
Hans Delbrück was a historian who studied at the University of Bonn (~1869–1873) and held a post at the University of Berlin in 1885.

Hans Harder is an Indologist who completed his Magister at the University of Heidelberg, followed by a doctorate under Rahul Peter Das and Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, where he served as an assistant (1995–2007).

Hans Hartog is an Indologist who studied at Tübingen, Bethel, Munich, and Marburg, completing his PhD at Marburg under Friedrich Heiler and receiving instruction from teachers including Walther Wüst and Hanns Oertel.

Hans Heinrich Schaeder worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (~1930–1931), the University of Berlin (~1931–1946), and the University of Göttingen (~1946–1957).

Hans Henrich Hock is a linguist and Indologist who completed graduate studies at Northwestern University and Yale University under Warren Cowgill. He became a Professor of Linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1967).
